input:
The logical statement [~(~p ∨ q) ∨ (p ∧ r)] ∧ (~q ∧ r) is equivalent to

Options:
A. (p ∧ r) ∧ ~q
B. (p ∧ ~q) ∨ r
C. ~p ∨ r
D. ~p ∧ r

phase_1_understand_the_problem.problem_restatement: Simplify the compound logical statement [~(~p ∨ q) ∨ (p ∧ r)] ∧ (~q ∧ r) to its equivalent form using standard logical laws.
phase_1_understand_the_problem.key_observation: Apply De Morgan's law to simplify ~(~p ∨ q) = p ∧ ~q, then use distributive, associative, and absorption laws step by step.

key_formulas.absorption: (A ∨ B) ∧ (A ∧ B) = A ∧ B  (the conjunction absorbs)

phase_3_plan_the_approach.strategy: Simplify inside-out: first apply De Morgan's law to ~(~p ∨ q), then use distributive law, then associative law, then absorption, and finally commutative law.
logical_steps: Step 1: Apply De Morgan's law to ~(~p ∨ q)
Step 2: Expand [·] using distributive law with (~q ∧ r)
Step 3: Apply associative law to regroup
Step 5: Apply commutative law to match option

step_4_absorption_law.reasoning: ~q ∧ r implies both ~q and r, which satisfies ~q ∨ r; so (X ∨ Y) ∧ (X ∧ Y) = X ∧ Y where X=~q, Y=r

phase_5_verify_answer.verification: De Morgan: ~(~p∨q) = p∧~q. Distributive: (p∧~q)∨(p∧r) = p∧(~q∨r). Then p∧(~q∨r)∧(~q∧r) = p∧(~q∧r) by absorption. Reordering gives (p∧r)∧~q ✓
